in_text_mentions: Physical examination revealed pruritic papules and pustules on the chest, back, and buttocks (Figures 1-3). Dermoscopy of a single lesion demonstrated a pustule with a central punctum on an erythematous base (Figure 4). Involved areas were occluded by swimwear when using the hot tub. A wound culture of a lesion on the back was collected. Clinical suspicion was for folliculitis, either by Staphylococcus aureus or P. aeruginosa. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of follicular papules and pustules in the axilla in a patient with culture-confirmed Pseudomonas aeruginosa folliculitis. B: Clinical photograph of erythematous follicular papules and pustules in the inguinal flexural area in Pseudomonas folliculitis. C: Dermoscopic image of a folliculocentric papule in a case of Pseudomonas folliculitis, with caption-supported pinkish background, paler centre, and central vellus hair.
panels.attribution_text: Errichetti and Stinco. Dermoscopy: a useful tool for assisting the diagnosis of Pseudomonas folliculitis.. Anais brasileiros de dermatologia 2016. doi:10.1590/abd1806-4841.20165382. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Physical examination revealing several erythemato-edematous papules and a few pustules on the right armpit (a) and inguinal area (b). Polarized light noncontact dermoscopic examination (X10 magnification) of a papule displays a pinkish background with a paler centre and a central thin vellus hair (black arrow); no distinct vessel is evident (c).

Physical examination revealed numerous erythemato-edematous papules and a few pustules (Figures 1A and 1B). On polarized light noncontact dermoscopic examination (DermLite DL3 x10; 3Gen, San Juan Capistrano, CA, USA), all the papules exhibited a pinkish background with a paler centre and a central vellus hair, thus highlighting the folliculocentric nature of the rash; no distinct vessel was evident (Figure 1C).
